title: Ten More Minutes
subject: a husband who sets the alarm ten minutes before it needs to go off every weekday so he and his wife can lie awake talking about nothing before the day starts
caption: Gospel-tinged piano folk-pop ballad, mid-2020s chart style. Upright piano playing slow rolling chords, fingerpicked acoustic guitar, a sustained cello line under the verses, a small gospel choir answering the last chorus, soft kick and handclaps on two and four. Intimate room mix with warm tape softness. Male tenor, hushed and close in the verses, opening to full voice in the choruses. 72 BPM, D major. Tender, warm and unhurried. No trap drums, no autotune, no EDM build, no country twang, no rock guitar solo.
lyrics:
[Intro - upright piano and cello]

[Verse 1]
Six-fifteen, the phone goes off
I set it early, on purpose
You don't even open your eyes
You just say morning to the pillow

[Chorus]
Give me ten more minutes
Talking nonsense in the dark
Like what we'd name a boat
Before the day knows where we are

[Verse 2]
You tell me what you saw asleep
I swear I was in it too
The heating ticks, the street is dark
Nobody needs us yet

[Chorus]
Give me ten more minutes
Still arguing about the boat
You want Margaret
I say Margaret's a coat

[Bridge - choir enters]
Thirty years from now
I'll still set it early

[Chorus]
Give me ten more minutes
Your cold foot on my shin
Ten more minutes
Then the day can come in

[Outro - piano alone]
Six-fifteen
Stay there, love
